recommendation.justification: Satellite imagery shows critical crop water stress (NDWI negative, NDVI 0.154) while soil pH and nitrogen are optimal. Rainfall is below the 1000‑2000 mm seasonal requirement, and low organic carbon threatens moisture retention and disease resistance. Prompt irrigation and soil amendment are needed to prevent major yield loss, and rising market prices make rapid recovery economically advantageous.
actions: Activate flood irrigation today to maintain a 5‑10 cm water layer across the rice field until soil moisture reaches field capacity.
Conduct on‑site scouting within 24 h for symptoms of blast, sheath blight, and nutrient deficiencies; record observations.
If disease symptoms are found, apply the recommended fungicide (e.g., tricyclazole) according to label rates.
Schedule supplemental irrigation every 2‑3 days (or as needed) to compensate for the rainfall deficit until the forecasted rains meet the 1000 mm minimum.
Incorporate 5‑10 t ha⁻¹ of well‑decomposed compost or organic manure within the next 7 days to raise organic carbon and improve water‑holding capacity.
Re‑measure soil moisture with a portable probe after each irrigation event and adjust water depth accordingly.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Restored soil moisture will improve canopy vigor, reduce the risk of disease‑related yield loss, and position the crop to capitalize on the current upward market trend, preserving profitability.

Soil moisture readings at 15 cm depth each morning.
Weekly NDVI/NDWI assessment via satellite or drone imagery.
Record any disease incidence and treatment actions.
Track market price updates weekly to plan optimal harvest timing.

steps.finding: Start immediate flood irrigation to relieve severe water stress, scout the field for disease and nutrient deficiencies, and amend soil with organic matter.
actions: Activate flood irrigation today to maintain a 5‑10 cm water layer across the rice field until soil moisture reaches field capacity.
Conduct on‑site scouting within 24 h for symptoms of blast, sheath blight, and nutrient deficiencies; record observations.
If disease symptoms are found, apply the recommended fungicide (e.g., tricyclazole) according to label rates.
Schedule supplemental irrigation every 2‑3 days (or as needed) to compensate for the rainfall deficit until the forecasted rains meet the 1000 mm minimum.
Incorporate 5‑10 t ha⁻¹ of well‑decomposed compost or organic manure within the next 7 days to raise organic carbon and improve water‑holding capacity.
Re‑measure soil moisture with a portable probe after each irrigation event and adjust water depth accordingly.
steps.justification: Satellite imagery shows critical crop water stress (NDWI negative, NDVI 0.154) while soil pH and nitrogen are optimal. Rainfall is below the 1000‑2000 mm seasonal requirement, and low organic carbon threatens moisture retention and disease resistance. Prompt irrigation and soil amendment are needed to prevent major yield loss, and rising market prices make rapid recovery economically advantageous.
